detail.claim: its rise reports in part cell arrival
detail.objection: Much of the bulk rise is neutrophil arrival and Mendelian randomisation is null, so the signal is weak evidence of a causal role.

detail.claim: Mendelian randomisation gives no support, and biopsies show no change
detail.objection: Prediction is tiny (+0.036 in NK cells), biopsies show no change and there is no clinical drug; the card itself concedes it stays only to fill the list.

detail.claim: long-term inhibition may reproduce that disease
detail.objection: Red safety light and complement's role in infection defence make chronic inhibition risky; an ex vivo test of the approved drug is still reasonable.

detail.claim: What is missing: any functional or genetic evidence
detail.objection: Reproducible and intrinsic, yet an intracellular enzyme with no extracellular part and a single list mention; it is a discovery bet, not an evidence-backed target.

detail.claim: which does not support the inhibition hypothesis in tissue
detail.objection: Ubiquitous mitochondrial gene, one instrument, predicted cell differs from single-cell cell, and inflamed biopsies show a slight decrease; inhibition is unsupported in tissue.

detail.claim: a transcription factor is hard to drug
detail.objection: Transcription factor, main source neutrophils and macrophages not the predicted dendritic cell, null genetics pointing the other way, and no clinical drug.

detail.claim: to see benefit and harm in one test
detail.objection: The parallel fibroblast and organoid test is the right design, as it reads benefit and harm together.

detail.claim: no Mendelian randomisation support and no change in biopsies
detail.objection: Tiny predicted effect, no change in biopsies, no genetic corroboration and no drug; confirming the variant effect on expression comes before any target claim.

detail.claim: its role in colitis-associated cancer is unsettled
detail.objection: Safety light is green, but the tumour-suppressor annotation and recent, single-group mouse data justify organoid work before any antibody.

detail.claim: its literature is one expression paper
detail.objection: Rises already in non-inflamed mucosa, and about 41% of the bulk rise is intrinsic; fibroblast silencing is a sensible first test, but the evidence base is thin.

detail.claim: blocking it would act on neutrophil recruitment rather than on a change of the tissue
detail.objection: Most of the bulk rise is composition; blocking one CXCR2 ligand among several may be compensated, and neutrophil clearance is needed for infection defence.

detail.claim: What is missing: any functional or genetic evidence
detail.objection: Rises in crypt cells as a possible repair programme, so inhibition could slow healing; an orphan P450 with no paper beyond a list mention.

detail.claim: a CFB loss-of-function variant linked to perianal Crohn's disease implies its function protects
detail.objection: A loss-of-function CFB variant that looks protective argues against inhibition, and a red safety light is not outweighed by a large epithelial rise; the test should read epithelial damage, as proposed.

detail.claim: What is missing: any functional or genetic evidence
detail.objection: Intrinsic epithelial rise and clean safety support a first knockdown, but with no paper beyond a list mention the case rests on expression alone.

detail.claim: its literature is one expression paper
detail.objection: The change survives adjustment and is already up in non-inflamed mucosa, but the biology of the protease in colitis is unknown, so the first experiment is exploratory.

detail.claim: so its role in colitis-associated cancer is unsettled
detail.objection: Epithelial, intrinsic and functionally supported, but described as a tumour suppressor, so long-term inhibition needs an explicit cancer read-out alongside the organoid test.

detail.claim: so the producing cell is not settled
detail.objection: Only 28% of the bulk rise is kept and the in-situ signal sits in smooth muscle, so the cell for the first experiment is uncertain; restoring BMP activity could also matter for epithelium.

detail.claim: an anti-P-selectin antibody did not significantly improve colitis
detail.objection: The card itself shows a null genetic test, a negative animal antibody result and an amber safety light; an approved drug alone does not justify the first slot.

detail.claim: administration of follistatin attenuated inflammatory cell infiltration
detail.objection: Follistatin, which neutralises activins, reduced histologic score and myeloperoxidase activity in TNBS and DSS colitis and in IL-10-deficient mice, supporting activin blockade.

detail.claim: it is strongly loss-constrained
detail.objection: A LOEUF of 0.17 and a lineage that does not replicate in any other atlas weigh against it; sotatercept is a ligand trap acting on several activins, not on INHBA alone.

detail.claim: Mendelian randomisation gives no support, and biopsies show no change
detail.objection: Every layer beyond the sequence prediction is null or absent; it is an inherited-risk hypothesis, not a first-year treatment target.

detail.claim: no Mendelian randomisation support and no change in biopsies
detail.objection: Only the sequence prediction supports it, so confirming the variant effect is a prerequisite, not a target test.

detail.claim: What is missing: any functional or genetic evidence
detail.objection: The card flags a possible repair programme; inhibiting it could impair healing, so the wound-healing arm of the experiment is essential and the gene is a screen, not a target.

detail.claim: so blocking it could slow repair
detail.objection: Crypt-zone rise with a repair programme flag and only biomarker papers; restoring rather than blocking may be the direction, which the organoid test with protein addition addresses.
